The accounting analysis wrote two adjustments, and the calculator applied both to quality-adjusted free cash flow only. The first removes the trailing net tax benefit, an amount of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted.adjustments_applied.0.amount}. The second counts Comtrafo's repaid debt, {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted.adjustments_applied.1.amount}, as acquisition cost. Together they take that measure from {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted.adjustments_applied.0.before} to {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted}. A caution on the first: the benefit was almost all deferred and never entered operating cash flow ({terms.trailing_four_quarters.operating_cash_flow}). Subtracting it from a cash measure removes cash that was never counted, so the adjusted figure overstates the drag. Neither adjustment would touch the DCF drivers, which start from operating margin. The tax benefit sits below the operating line, and the debt repayment is a past financing flow. One item does sit inside operating income: the non-cash earnout gain that MD&A reports for the quarter. It carries no adjustment because its amount is not in the calculator. The drivers handle it instead: the base year-one margin is set below the trailing {ratios.profitability.operating_margin|pct} and slightly below the fiscal year ended March 2026 ({earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_margin|pct}).
